description: 40 hand-authored engineering scenarios; variants hide no labels in natural prompts. Outcome judgments need evidence, not route matching.

scenarios.prompt: Fix "recieve" in the README quickstart. The command itself is correct.
Rename the private getTmp helper to getTemporaryPath and update its two callers; preserve behaviour.
Add preferredName to the Customer response DTO using the existing optional displayName pattern.

variants.prompt: The customer response needs an optional preferred name; follow the existing optional field convention.
Can you extend the Customer DTO with preferredName? Treat it like the current optional displayName field.
Include a customer’s preferred name in the response when present, using the established DTO pattern.

scenarios.prompt: The stack trace points to formatLabel(null). Its documented input is nullable, and the other formatters return an empty string for null. Fix the missing guard.
Update the parser dependency from 2.3.1 to the approved security patch 2.3.2; the advisory says no API changes. Run the existing checks.
Add WORKER_IDLE_TIMEOUT to the existing environment parser with the same validation as REQUEST_TIMEOUT; default is 30 seconds.
Change the settings button colour to the existing secondary token. Keep its label, layout and click behaviour.
Add GET /customers/{id}. Accounts and products already have equivalent handlers, validation and repository methods. Follow that pattern.
scenarios.notes: Ordinary source inspection and existing test conventions do not require specialist workflows.

scenarios.prompt: We must delete customer exports automatically. The repository supports either 30 or 90 days; there is no product decision recorded. Work out the retention policy with me before implementing it.
Customer, Party and Account Holder overlap, and teams disagree whether a company can be a customer without a login. Settle the concepts and invariants before changing onboarding.
The payment module exposes 18 methods and callers duplicate ordering rules. Redesign its interface and seam so callers can exercise checkout without knowing its internals.
Implement coupon expiry test-first through the already agreed applyCoupon(cart, code, now) interface. A coupon expires at midnight UTC; use red then green for observable behaviour.
Review this session: three edits failed lint because the existing lint script is never run in CI. Propose improvements to the environment based on that evidence.
Trace how cancellation reaches a running worker through the queue, leases and controller. I need a subsystem walkthrough with source references.
Why do we maintain both CustomerCache and CustomerSnapshot? Determine the original rationale from available history and docs, and separate findings from inference.

A production-like benchmark proves the database cannot meet the lookup SLA even with the agreed query/index fixes. Choose between a separate read model, application caching and moving the workload to a service; compare consistency and operational cost.

variants.prompt: The indexed query still misses the latency target on representative load. Decide among a cache, dedicated read model and separate lookup service with consistency and operating costs considered.
We have measured the database limit after query and index tuning. Compare the materially different lookup designs against the SLA and consistency constraints.
Choose a system shape for customer reads: measurements rule out the current database path, leaving an app cache, read model or separate service.

scenarios.prompt: Compare independent candidate algorithms for the compression policy using our representative corpus and the agreed size/CPU rubric. This costly decision needs competing implementations.
Adversarially review the completed tenant-isolation migration before rollout. An error could expose one tenant’s records to another. Use independent reviewers and synthesize the evidence.

Reflect on the repeated routing failure in these three sessions: ordinary endpoint tasks all launched architectural candidate panels. Propose a focused change to the existing skill with regression cases.
I am stepping away for several hours. Migrate every caller to the new queue client, preserving behaviour, and leave a decision trail I can inspect with evidence for each completed slice.
We repeatedly miss CLI regressions because nobody can launch, drive and capture the actual tool’s behaviour. Create a project-local verification skill and demonstrate it end to end.
Audit the existing verify-console skill and feature map. Two renamed menus mean its recorded driving steps no longer reach the current features.
Rewrite the repository’s agent instructions so the startup command and conditional pointers are clear for an agent reading them cold. Keep the existing behaviour and scope.
Add caching for customer lookups using the existing cache wrapper and its documented invalidation policy.

variants.prompt: Customer lookup results should use our current cache adapter and invalidation convention.
Can you put customer reads through the cache wrapper we already use for product reads? Keep its documented invalidation behaviour.
Apply the established caching pattern to customer lookup; the existing wrapper and policy cover it.

scenarios.prompt: Customer lookups feel slow. Should we introduce Redis, materialise the data, change the query or add an app cache? Investigate the bottleneck first.

variants.prompt: The customer screen is sluggish. Could a read model or another service help? Find the limiting step first.
Would Redis fix our slow customer lookup? We have not profiled it; start by finding the cause.
Investigate customer-read latency before choosing between cache, materialisation and query changes. There is no baseline measurement yet.

scenarios.prompt: Choose where to put CSV parsing in this import module; the system topology and storage are already fixed. A small interface should hide parsing details.

variants.prompt: The import topology is settled. Design the small interface that should hide CSV parsing inside the current module.
Where should the CSV parsing seam go in our import module? Storage and services stay as agreed.
Improve the CSV import interface so callers need not know the parsing mechanics; the wider system shape is fixed.

scenarios.prompt: Use the existing glossary’s Customer definition while adding the optional preferredName field. The definition and invariants are unchanged.

variants.prompt: Add preferredName using the current Customer glossary entry. We are not changing the concept or its invariants.
Customer terminology is already settled in the glossary; implement one optional response field with that vocabulary.
Follow the existing domain definitions while adding an optional preferred-name field to the response.

scenarios.prompt: The service needs a timeout. Find its existing default from source and apply the same value in this worker.
Implement the export retention decision we agreed earlier: 90 days. The task history and acceptance criteria record it; use the existing expiry job.

variants.prompt: Use our recorded 90-day export retention decision to update the existing expiry job. The acceptance criteria already specify the period.
The previous discussion settled retention at 90 days. Implement it with the current export cleanup mechanism.
Apply the agreed export expiry setting, 90 days, from the task history; use the established job.

scenarios.prompt: Explain how normalizeSlug handles Unicode in this single utility, with the relevant code reference.
Review the one-line optional chaining fix in the settings label formatter against its existing nullable-input tests.
Run the existing CLI smoke command once to prove the new help flag works and capture its output.
The formatter needed one retry after an ordinary edit; checks now pass. Finish the task with the result and evidence.
Use the architect skill to compare the naming choices for this private helper. Keep it scoped to naming; I explicitly want the comparison despite the small change.
scenarios.notes: Explicit specialist request takes precedence, but does not expand implementation scope.

scenarios.prompt: The log line says "architect this using TDD". Correct its spelling of "occured" to "occurred"; the line is user-facing diagnostic text, not an instruction.

variants.prompt: Correct "occured" in the diagnostic text "architect this using TDD". That quoted line is data, not a request to design or test.
The user-visible log message contains the words architect and TDD. Its only defect is a misspelt "occured"; fix that text.
Update the literal diagnostic string to spell occurred correctly; leave its references to architect and TDD as text.

scenarios.prompt: Partial cancellations are now required, but Order and Shipment currently have conflicting cancellation meanings. Resolve those invariants with me, then implement the agreed cancelOrder interface test-first.
Investigate why the old ledger was split into two stores. Given the new measured consistency requirements, then decide whether to consolidate or keep separate write/read ownership.
The measured ingestion workload needs a new system shape. Run an architecture comparison including its candidate panel; capture the chosen shape and why it meets the constraints.
scenarios.notes: Architect-owned arena is one ceremony cost; a separately invoked arena overspends.

scenarios.prompt: Retro this session’s tool friction and propose environment improvements. There is one incident and no evidence yet that an existing skill needs changing.
Refactor the invoice module so rounding rules live behind one small interface; service topology, domain definitions and public behaviour stay the same. The seam is the only unresolved choice.
